data.table: Direct drive, or motor per joint
rows: A high-DOF hand reporting dozens of channels at several hundred hertz can crowd out the rest of the robot on a classic CAN bus. Ask for payload size and update rate before you put the hand and the arm on one segment.
The hand typically consumes roughly 10–20% of available wrist payload as a rule of thumb — treat that as approximate and work backwards from the arm rather than forwards from the grip.
Any compliant transmission moves over time. Ask whether joint offsets get re-zeroed in software or mechanically, and how often.
Ask what wears, what the spare costs and how long it takes. Swapping a finger module and re-stringing a cable are very different maintenance commitments.
Confirm the SDK, ROS packages and protocol support before comparing anything else. Our seven-day sample evaluation protocol covers what to test in week one.
